title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — die/created/ejected in Adam without those acts imputed
pass_a_gloss: We may be said created, just, blessed, or cast from paradise in Adam without those acts being imputed. So 'sinned in him' can mean only that he passed nature and sin to us by natural generation.
pass_b_english: We can be said to have been created in Adam, to have been created just and blessed, to have been cast out of paradise, and so on, and yet neither his creation, nor original righteousness, nor casting out of paradise is imputed to us. Therefore we could be said to have sinned in him, in the way we can be said to have been in him, because he communicated to us both his nature and his sin by natural propagation.
source_text: Dici possumus in Adamo creati fuisse, creati fuisse iusti & beati, eiecti fuisse e paradiso &c., nec tamen eius creatio, aut iustitia originalis, aut eiectio e paradiso nobis imputatur. Potuimus ergo dici in eo peccasse, quomodo dici possumus in eo fuisse, quia ille quam naturam tam peccatum suum nobiscum communicavit propagatione naturali.

choices.choice: Other in-Adam phrases without imputation; sin passed by propagation
